topics.title: UN speeches put diplomacy on stage
topics.summary: World leaders used the UN General Assembly to press competing views on security, climate, trade, and diplomacy during a tense week in New York.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone gets one big UN speech, who uses it to persuade people and who accidentally turns it into a group chat argument?

topics.title: Markets watch oil rebound
topics.summary: U.S. stocks slipped from near-record levels as Brent crude rebounded above $100 and bond yields rose after a stronger economic report.
topics.discussionPrompt: When oil prices bounce and stocks get twitchy, who starts reading charts and who just asks if gas is about to get annoying?

topics.title: Doordash settles New York pay case
topics.summary: DoorDash agreed to pay $131.5 million after New York investigators said delivery workers were underpaid, a settlement the company acknowledged publicly.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an app has to pay workers back, who focuses on fairness and who starts wondering how many tiny fees were involved?

topics.title: Climate action questions reach UN week
topics.summary: Climate advocates are watching whether the next UN leader will keep climate action central as governments debate energy security, costs, and accountability.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the UN gets a new boss, who wants climate at the top of the inbox and who says every crisis is already in the inbox?

topics.title: AI looms over Trump-Xi meeting
topics.summary: AI, trade, and strategic trust are expected to feature heavily as Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare for high-stakes talks.
topics.discussionPrompt: When leaders talk about AI, who pictures chips and rules, and who pictures two people pretending the future fits on an agenda?

topics.title: China expands AI data centers
topics.summary: BBC reports huge data centers are rising quickly in Inner Mongolia as China races to power its AI ambitions and compete with the U.S.
topics.discussionPrompt: If AI needs whole landscapes of data centers, who is impressed by the engineering and who asks about the electricity bill?

topics.title: Paris dig points to ancient settlement
topics.summary: Archaeologists found an ancient wall beneath Paris that officials say could help confirm the site of the city’s first settlement.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a city finds an ancient wall under itself, who wants a museum tour and who wants to know what else is under the sidewalk?

topics.title: Offshore wind dispute heads to court
topics.summary: California and New York sued the Trump administration over plans to buy back offshore wind leases, escalating a fight over U.S. energy priorities.
topics.discussionPrompt: When wind projects turn into a courtroom story, who talks clean energy and who talks about who gets to steer the power grid?

topics.title: Debt costs worry global institutions
topics.summary: The IMF and other major institutions warned that rising debt and borrowing costs are pressuring governments, including the U.S. and UK.
topics.discussionPrompt: If countries have budget stress like households do, who says tighten spending and who says the spreadsheet needs imagination?

topics.title: Rubik's Cube record turns heads
topics.summary: A six-year-old broke a women’s world Rubik’s Cube record, giving a lighter moment to a busy international news day.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a six-year-old solves a cube faster than adults can find their keys, who celebrates and who quietly hides their puzzle?
